title: Sampling Interval Trade-off Bench
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Five continuous signals sampled at six intervals, showing the true signal, the reconstruction a CSV reader would see, which annotated events were missed, the storage and power cost of each interval, and a verdict that depends on the stated monitoring purpose.

learningObjectives: Justify a sampling interval for a stated monitoring purpose.
Weigh captured detail against file size, power and SD card wear.
Identify an event that a given interval misses entirely.
State why dense data can be thinned but sparse data cannot be enriched.
prerequisites: Chapter 14: sampling interval, storage and card endurance
Chapters 9, 10 and 11 for the cloud, gust and P wave events

keyQuestions: What is the fastest thing you actually need to see?
Is 60 seconds a good interval? Good for what?
What does a year of data at this interval cost in megabytes?
If you are unsure, should you sample faster or slower than you think you need?
commonMisconceptions: There is one correct sampling interval for a weather station.
Storage capacity is the reason not to sample quickly.
Data that has gaps in an event can be interpolated back.
assessmentOpportunities: Records the sample count inside an event at each interval.
Explains why one interval is adequate for one purpose and not another.
Defends a chosen interval against detail, volume and card wear together.
